[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/41a4435c561da5d7fa8d56d80f174104b8c2fa57.png[/img]
The M4 Sherman is the big brother and originator of the Firefly, the previous predominant Allied tank in Brass Brigade. It features a larger profile, but stronger armor. The extra protection from damage comes at a disadvantage though, as the Sherman is slower than the Firefly. However, the extra weight and reduced speed do make it more stable for turning at high speeds. Look for this tank on maps that feature either the Americans or British, such as Anzio, Caen, El Alamein, and Battleaxe.

The T-34-76 needs no introduction. It was one of the longest produced tanks in history with a production count of almost 2-to-1 against the M4 Sherman. Compared to the T-34-85 (previously the only Russian tank in Brass Brigade), the 76 features a shorter barrel, slightly larger profile, stronger armor, reduced speed, and more suspension travel for traversing uneven terrain. Look for these on maps that Feature Russian troops, such as Kursk, Stalingrad, and Ponyri.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/0b6dd173b28909284a4e413293aa91583533c5d2.png[/img]
The StuG is perhaps the quirkiest tank in Brass Brigade. To aid the Axis forces against their new Allied armor opposition, the StuG features an extremely low profile, moderate speed, and very high resilience to incoming shells. Sounds too good to be true? The StuG comes with two big drawbacks - it does not have a driver-operated machine gun and its turret cannot rotate horizontally. The StuG must face directly at its target. This makes the StuG ideal as a support tank from the rear while other tanks charge forward. These can be found on almost all maps featuring the German forces.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/4b4600de51db7cc5111a3ca4587b4ffa42c1f4be.png[/img]
Avanti! The Italians are an often under-represented part of WW2 history and a good amount of players have asked for their inclusion into Brass Brigade. You can now be on the lookout for Italian blackshirt troops in the Anzio Day 1 and Day 2 maps fighting along-side the Germans. They sport Carcano rifles and Beretta pistols as their go-to weapons.

[b]The Italians aren't a fully flushed out faction; I see them more as a complementary part of the German forces for their inclusion into Brass Brigade.[/b] Brass Brigade features a map with British and American forces fighting together and I think the idea of Italian and German forces fighting together should be just as welcome - it helps to highlight the global scale of WW2 and the comradery these nations might have had to employ.

[i]*Note - I've also seen lots of people asking for other factions to be included into the game. While I wish I could include every faction that took part in WW2, I simply cannot afford to do so. I have to be picky when it comes to what I spend my time developing - seeing as how I already had maps on the Italian Front, I felt they were the best choice for inclusion.[/i]

[h1]Map Update - The Battle of Caen[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/9dd29b7a3cb01d9055bad7221c978c8aded48f0b.png[/img]
Caen has had a new area added just outside the hedgerows near the Allied and Axis spawns. This area contains a small trench network, a crashed cargo plane, and 3 new flags to capture. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/f7c49753003de1927f1a9015f003349091a7eea2.png[/img]
This area helps to spread out the armor on the map and helps ease up the action in the town's center courtyard area. More flanking routes are possible by both sides and it adds some more visual variety to the map. The foliage outside the playable area has also been greatly reduced which should increase performance for some users. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/ac72e167fd2d35fedf5d8cffe1f49ea2194dfe62.png[/img]

[h1]Map Update - Anzio[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/ea81e452ba398c9ba282e0524b5d4cccfa800566.png[/img]
The American forces on Anzio have struggled to hold the main town area against the Germans - the Destroyed House outpost is behind the main ridgeline and offers little cover to the advancing Americans. A new capture point has been added opposite the ridge giving the Americans a chance to take and hold the main town center. Speed is key for them to take and hold the town.

The AI has seen several tweaks to how they navigate and move. Artificial intelligence and NPC movement is a never-ending battle with a game that has open maps and non-predetermined pathfinding. I'm actively watching how the bots perform with these changes and initial impressions seem good - let me know your feedback as you play so I can adjust further!

Attention Brass Brigade Soldiers!

[h1]General Covid-19 Status Update & Regards[/h1]
Welcome to another Brass Brigade update. First, let me start by once again thanking each and every one of you for supporting Brass Brigade. Let me also extend my best wishes for good health to each and every one of you during this unfortunate Covid-19 pandemic. I have been self-isolating for well over a month (as many have) and I'm trying my best to balance time spent on the computer for my day job, working on Brass Brigade, and other non screen-related activities. I hope you are all making the best of the situation and following the recommendations of your local health authorities.

As mentioned in previous updates, the self-isolation requirements where I live make consistent working on Brass Brigade difficult simply due to spending so much time programming each and every day without being able to go about my formerly normal routine. Work has slowed but hopefully this update gives you some fun new gameplay experiences. I'll do my best to continue working throughout the isolation period, and I hope you are all also finding a healthy work/life balance for your current situation. Without further a-do, let's discuss what's new in this update. (You can get a quick summary of Brass Brigade's newest features in this Spring Recap trailer too!)

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1q_hHNZ6NTA

 [h1]Troop Command System[/h1]
[h2]The Basics[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/fa6741ac7b4c5a3bb2167297e9a488a6d5e0dfc9.png[/img]
[i]Issuing orders to a German squad.[/i]

For a long time, players have been asking for smarter bots and specifically - the ability to command bots. I'm happy to say that you can now issue a suite of basic commands to nearby bots in-game. The simple system lets you recruit nearby allies to join your squad which you can then issue three different orders to. [b]After recruiting some allies, you can order them to follow you, move to a specific position, or hold at your current position.[/b] You can also tell the bots to take cover (crouch/prone) and get back up at any time. At any time, you can recruit other nearby stray allies to join your squad - they will immediately begin executing your most recent order. If you decide that the burden of command is too much to bear, you can dismiss all the allies under your current command; they will then return to battle like normal. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/0ded055574c1ccd6cde74395c1f07ce4fb743f57.png[/img]
[i]Officers have the largest sphere-of-influence for recruiting allies.[/i]

You can begin recruiting allies and issuing orders through the command-rose UI (Default Key: X). Any time a bot is recruited, a color-coded orb will appear above them. The color of the orb matches the colors of the orders in the command-rose UI and indicates the current order they are executing. You can see your latest order at the top of the command rose as well. If any further bots are recruited, they will execute that order immediately. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/92f1c309967d6f0d4991b1b59ad8aac1374db6c8.png[/img]
[i]A blue arrow denotes where your bots are moving to when issued the move order.[/i]

[h2]Notes[/h2]
If the player dies, all commanded bots will be dismissed, same as if you dismissed them manually. While there is no limit to the number of bots that the player can recruit to their squad, not all bots can be recruited. Specialized bots (such as rocketeers, banzai, sniper, and tank drivers) cannot be recruited. They will go about their usual behaviors. 

Another noteworthy point is that different roles have differing recruitment ranges. Officers have a larger recruitment radius. Squad leaders and commando-type roles have medium sized ranges. Rifleman and support roles have the smallest range. You can see the distance of your influence projected around you when you attempt to recruit allies.  

You can come up with some creative scenarios with these basics commands. You can collect a group of bots and have them follow you while attacking a base. You can stay back and send them to attack on your behalf. Or you tell them to hold a specific position while you rush around a flank. I'm sure you'll come up with other tactical situations that were previously just not possible with the older AI patterns.

[h1]Quality of Life Improvements[/h1]
There have been a number of smaller quality of life improvements sprinkled throughout the game. Some more noteworthy examples are...
[h2]Animation[/h2]
- Certain animations for characters (such as issuing orders) now do not lower the player's weapon, affecting the player's aim. Player weapons remain centered more consistently as a result.
[h2]Audio[/h2]
- Reduced frequency of bullet-snapping sound effect.
- New sound effects for SVT-40 & SVT-40 Scoped Rifle.
- Fixed a bug which caused dead bots to still play vocal cues.
[h2]Controls[/h2]
- Inverting the Y-Axis now affects tank aiming controls as well.
[h2]Gameplay: Weapons[/h2]
- Pistols have had an accuracy reduction across the board.
- Grenades & TNT have had a damage increased across the board.
- Grenades & TNT have had their explosion radius slightly increased across the board.
- All weapons now have much more realistic bullet ballistic speeds; bullets are generally slower than they were before.
[h2]Gameplay: AI[/h2]
- Bot accuracy has seen a general decrease across the board.
- American bots have been buffed slightly with regards to their health values.
- Bots may stop/crouch while shooting and hold position before continuing. This helps to reduce the "always charging" effect from before. 
[h2]Optimization[/h2]
- Reducing bullet speeds have lead to reduced load on the physics engine, increasing performance slightly.
- Adjustments to internal tick rates to bot calculations and physics processes have yielded slight performance improvements on my test systems; your results may vary.
- Adjustments to audio compression parameters should reduce the amount of audio clipping that occurs during very loud moments.

[h1]The Future[/h1]
I am considering adding another map or two to the game while continuing with general quality-of-life improvements. I have some other ideas that are a bit larger in scale, and I may tinker with to see how well they fit in with the overall code-base and feel of the game. Unfortunately, I don't have much I'm willing to disclose at this time; my updates have just about caught up with my thinking. 

[h1]Wrapping Up[/h1]
I hope you enjoy the new command system and general improvements to the game. Feel free to swing by our Discord or the Steam Discussion forum for Brass Brigade if you have some suggestions, feedback, or other related interests. Feel free to leave a review (especially if you're loving the game) on the Steam Store Page - they really do help!

Until next time,
Henry Kucab

notes.title: Troop Command System Sneak Peek - Brass Brigade
notes.content:
Hello soldiers,

First, let me start by saying that I hope everyone is doing okay given the current Covid-19 situation. It's my hope that everyone is as healthy as they can be. Remember to minimize unnecessary travel, practice social distancing, and wash your hands!

[h1]Update about Brass Brigade Development[/h1]
For those of you who do not know, Brass Brigade is made by one person - me. I work at one of the Big Three American Automotive manufacturers and I (like many others), am working from home for the foreseeable future. Fortunate as I am to be able to keep my day job, I am now required to spend the majority of my day programming from home for work, which makes it difficult to then pivot and continue working on Brass Brigade in the evenings. The inability to conduct other activities outside of my house means that I am being very careful to balance the amount of time I spend working on my computer with other activities that give my mind, eyes, and hands a break from keyboard & screen. What this means is that development of Brass Brigade has slowed down as I work to limit my screen time. Rest assured that work is still continuing, but it won't be continuing at the rate that I was able to move at earlier. I hope you understand my need to balance my health and screen time with my desire to bring you guys more Brass Brigade. It's a strange time indeed. With that said, I do want to show you what I have been inching towards over these last few weeks.

[h1]Troop Commanding[/h1]
I have been working to add in basic troop commands to Brass Brigade. The player can bring up a command-rose widget and issue orders to nearby troops. Once a troop is under the player's influence, they will remain so until they die, the player dies, or they are dismissed. At the moment, the player can tell troops to follow them, move to a specific point, hold at the player's current position, and be dismissed (go back to behaving like normal). 

While these behaviors may be changed/tweaked as time goes on, even these basic commands open up fun side-avenues of strategy and gameplay scenarios. You can gather a group of bots to follow you around a flank that bots don't normally take. You can get a group of bots to hold a point with you instead of rushing out into the fray. You can send them to attack a point and cover them from your vantage point. The list goes on.

[previewyoutube=5yruhkc07Rw;full][/previewyoutube]

I've made a short video that showcases the current state of the troop commanding. The art is very basic & placeholder in some areas, but the bot functionality works fairly well at this stage of development. I hope you enjoy watching and please, feel free to offer any feedback you may have. I'm looking to start simple with this feature and develop it over time. 

The release date of this feature is still TBD.

[h2]Performance Bump[/h2]
A very strange but sensible performance increase was achieved in the game by slowing down bullet projectile speeds to better match their real world counterparts. By slowing down the speed of bullets to better match their real-world speeds, the space the physics engine needs to analyze for collisions is smaller frame-to-frame. Less time spent calculating physics means a higher average frame-rate. 

[h1]The Future[/h1]
For the time being, we must do all we can to curb the spread of Covid-19. I will continue to work on Brass Brigade when I can. Stay healthy & safe everyone!

Until next time,
Henry K.

notes.title: Take aim! Sniper Rifles and FPS Improvements Now Available in this Free Update!
notes.content:
[h1]Heads down! Sniper![/h1]

I'd like to again thank you for being loyal soldiers in the Brass Brigade. As some of you may know, I have teased the forthcoming sniper rifle update for a bit and I am glad to say that they have finally arrived! Alongside these highly lethal rifles comes a host of other tweaks, bug fixes, and updated controls to further refine your gameplay experience. Without further a-do, let's dive into the world of sharpshooting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/047aa79b180621c3a4b4b640e944af4a82e44864.png[/img]
[i]Did someone ask for Pvt. Jackson?[/i]

[h1]Sniper Rifles[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/59113a53eaaa79ed736430912b1c3d9c28a3a62d.jpg[/img]
[i]The No. 4 and a break in the trees is all a sniper really needs...[/i]

The US, Soviets, Germans, and British have had new sniper rifles added in this update. Each army has either one or more classes that comes equipped with a weapon that has a telescopic sight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/9aaf1ec4162a8575edb58d403a4eab6ffbb7d216.jpg[/img]
[i]Aiming in 3rd person (left) vs aiming in 1st person (right) with sniper rifles[/i]

[b]In order to use the scope, you must first switch to first person mode and then aim as you normally would. Aiming in third-person mode zooms in over-the-shoulder just like normal[/b]; this was done to make close-combat a viable option with these sniper rifles for the player. Taking out targets at a distance naturally takes a bit more deliberate aim, and thus, affords you the ability to switch to first person and then aim with the scope. As with all weapons in Brass Brigade, the bullets are affected by gravity, and you will have to lead your shots if your target is far enough away from you. Sniper rifle bullets also leave a slightly more noticeable tracer effect through the air to help you locate enemy sharpshooters. But beware - sniper rifles are extremely powerful and their shooters are fairly accurate.

[h1]Sniper Bots[/h1]
To complement these new weapons, bots that wield sniper rifles have unique behavior. While they may still be caught in the middle of tense firefights and have to fight their way out like any other soldier, they prefer to find advantageous positions throughout the battlefields. They take up positions typically on high perches, on ridges, in tree lines, or towards the edges of the combat area. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/97931cfdd5a9dc3604122922b91b79bb4c226ada.png[/img]
[i]A Soviet sniper covers the "Wrecked Plane" flag on "Ponyri Apocalypse" from afar.[/i]

They cover an area for a bit and then rotate to a different area; good snipers don't stay in one spot too long. So keep your eyes open and watch for their distinct tracers, they are crack shots and try to hide in vegetation and other bits of cover.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/1ee548085c8f05957d00dd636a69b6c02d599a50.jpg[/img]
[i]A German sniper stays behind at Arnhem to counter-snipe.[/i]

[h1]Refined Mouse Movement[/h1]
To further refine the sniping and general shooting in Brass Brigade, some new mouse options have been added to the Controls menu. These include...
[list]
[*][b]Mouse Smoothing Toggle[/b]. This controls whether or not the mouse movement is filtered and smoothed. Originally, this was on by default, but you can now disable this if you wish. It results in snappier, raw mouse movement.
[*][b]Scope Sensitivity Multiplier Slider[/b]. This slider controls by what multiplier your sensitivity is multiplied with when aiming through a scope. Typically, you want smoother movement when zoomed in so much with a scope, so you can adjust this until you are happy with the relative sensitivity of being scoped vs. unscoped. 
[/list]

[h1]First Person Mode Weapon Stuttering Fixed[/h1]
In previous builds, when having switched to first person mode, the player's weapon model could "stutter" or "jitter" back and forth. This was caused by a de-sync problem between the timing of when the camera would update its position and when the player model would update its position. This has been corrected and now the camera and player are synced once the switch from 3rd person to 1st person finishes. You will notice that first person mode will feel crisper and more responsive here compared to its first implementation. 

[h1]Map Visual Iterations[/h1]
[h2]Omaha Beach Tweaks[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/14a1af20d059358d63838384bcdc109d200e0068.jpg[/img]
[list]
[*] Omaha Beach and Kursk have received some visual tweaks, mostly with regards to their skyboxes and lighting. Omaha Beach has switched from an orange-ish morning to a more hazy morning, to better reflect most people's perceptions of the battle. 
[*] There is a new capture point right below the bunkers called "The Shingle" which starts neutral. The allies can usually capture this quickly, which gives them a little bit of breathing room and helps get them off the beach.
[*] There is now a way for the player and bots to get up the cliff from the far right side.
[*] Allies now have 2 tanks that are available for them in Higgins boats.
[/list]

[h2]Kursk Tweaks[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/1ea0512977ca8ab44ff95247deb30b79dcb71cba.png[/img]
[list]
[*]Kursk has had a significant change from it's pale blue sky to a dark sunburst red-purple with a bit of distant fog added. 
[/list]
[h3]Other Map Tweaks [/h3][list]
[*][b]Port En Bessin[/b] - One of the capture points in the town has been moved closer to the British spawn to improve timings and the ability for the British to hold part of the town.
[*][b]Anzio - Day 1[/b] - Allies now have 1 tank that is available for them in a Higgins boat.
[/list]

[h1]Wrapping up...[/h1]
There are other quality of life improvements in this update too, such as updated weapon icons at the spawn menu (such as unique pictures for the M1928 Thompson and M1A1 Thompson, for example). Bullets that fly close to your head will make a snapping sound. The sniper rifles have new sound effects and there have been other goings-on under the hood. I am still looking into giving the player the ability to command nearby troops and tweaking the AI overall. I am also interested in exploring more special abilities for the different classes. These are next on my list of things to do, but the exact details of how they might work remain to be seem. That's game-dev for ya! Until then, I hope this update will make your experience even better!

[h1]Spread the Word![/h1]
If you've enjoyed Brass Brigade, please leave a review on the Steam Store Page - they do help! And please spread the word to your friends, communities, and anyone else who you think might enjoy playing Brass Brigade. My ability to continue bringing you updates and content is driven by my joy in seeing people play Brass Brigade and talking about it with fellow soldiers. Drop by our [url=https://discordapp.com/invite/DMdGBPc]Discord[/url] if you want to chat!

Until next time,
Henry K,

notes.title: Arnhem Incremental Update: Basic Spectator Camera Added
notes.content:
Hello troops,

A quick update from headquarters; In an attempt to continuously develop and continuously deliver features to you, rather than waiting for a single massive update, I bring to you an update with 2 key features.

[h1]Small Bug Fix[/h1]
The Arnhem Update has been positively received by most players, and I'm happy to hear you're all enjoying the new map and the airborne spawn for the British, However, a bug was noticed where sometimes the parachute for bots would not disappear after they had landed, and the chute would follow them around wherever they went. I believe the root cause of this has been found and the problem addressed. I will be watching this as I would like to continue to use airborne spawns if I decide to make other maps for which it would be appropriate (no promises of any specific maps at this time). 

[h1]Simple Spectator Camera[/h1]
Some users have asked for the ability to spectate a battle. I have added a simple spectator camera button under the "Deploy" button on the Redeploy screen. You can fly around the map without any restrictions; the camera has no collision or limits. You can watch the battle from any angle and enjoy some really cinematic/beautiful moments!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/8aea77a3b52aaee8e677bde52011747f9bed02fe.png[/img]
[i]You can watch battles unfold through the spectator camera from any angle![/i]


[h2]A Personal Note about Unlocking the Spectator Camera...[/h2]
Yes, you can even fly to parts of the level I never intended anyone to go, and you can even fly under/outside of the level. While some may think an entirely unlocked camera is a bit crude, I have a different belief. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/e17ac3da1bf4c00884f21d95363af7bc89796551.png[/img]
[i]Anzio - Day 2 from really, really, really far away. You weren't supposed to see this![/i]

One of my absolute favorite things I ever did when playing games back in my youth was to see things the developers didn't intend for me to see. I would try to tilt cameras a certain way to expose hidden parts of a level or to see the magic and trickery that was creating the virtual world I was inhabiting. It is with that same spirit that I leave the spectator camera unlocked. You can fly around, see all the rough edges, hidden bodies, and tricks that are used in Brass Brigade. I hope those of you that have any passion or interest in game development enjoy this little nod to my own childhood. I love learning how things work, and you can now take a peek at some of the things I never meant for anyone to see....just don't bother me about these rough edges (I'm trusting all of you!), I'm only human :)

[h1]The Future[/h1]
Snipers are currently in the works. Sniper weapon functionality is pretty solid at this time. I still need to create the scope overlays that are correct for each weapon (I'm using ugly placeholders at this time) and I'm even working to make bots with sniper rifles seek out advantageous positions and engage their targets from a distance; they shouldn't be running into the fray like their SMG-toting comrades.

Until next time,
Henry

notes.title: Heads up! Drop into the Battle of Arnhem with this Free Update TODAY!
notes.content:
Hello again troops of the [i]Brass Brigade[/i],

Today I'm happy to add another iconic WW2 battle into Brass Brigade's repertoire. For those of you who read the previous announcement (read it [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1163910/announcements/detail/1708488318656649754]here[/url]), you will already know which battle it is. For those of you who didn't, let's catch you up!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/2e108fd3369d9656a70907a71e477df51ac7dbaf.png[/img]

[h1]The Battle of Arnhem[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/42abc42d0d18a1a40678f8d47490ff423526b0ac.jpg[/img]
The Battle of Arnhem was a culmination of everything that went wrong for the allies during Operation Market Garden. Known as the largest airborne operation up to that point during WWII, allied troops from the United States, Britain, Poland, Canada, and the Netherlands attempted to capture nine bridges leading straight into Northern Germany. Paratroopers would land at each bridge and hold it until armored reinforcements could reach them, clearing the way in between each bridge. Speed and timing were key in achieving success, and the failure of even one unit to hold their position would result in further units being stranded. Unbeknownst to the allies - who thought their only opposition would be ineffective German infantry - the Germans stationed several Panzer groups nearby. The resulting carnage saw the paratroopers fending off Tigers tanks with small arms and light armor of their own. At the northern-most town of Arnhem, British troops found themselves outgunned and over 60 miles away from reinforcements. As seen in the 1977 film "A Bridge Too Far", the British would eventually falter and succumb to the German counter-attack. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/c531279b9a1e83eff39246af864492984f6dd294.png[/img]
However, Brass Brigade now offers you the opportunity to not only experience this iconic battle, but to potentially change the outcome of the battle. British troops drop into the fields behind Arnhem and must secure the area leading to the bridge before moving across the bridge itself. However, German troops on the opposite side of the river observe the paratroopers' advance and spring into a rapid assault, crossing the bridge into Arnhem. Both sides will meet on the bridge and must prevent their enemy from crossing. Once one side gains a successful foothold on the opposite side, the end of the battle usually follows soon after. Will you succeed in holding the bridge as the British? Or will you counter-attack as the Germans and attempt to root out the stream of British paratroopers from the beautifully calm skies that once owned the Dutch countryside?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/3a71eca595b6f3f9bfd3dec9c72fc2b0d4732378.png[/img]

[h1]Other New Art[/h1]
There have been other developments in the art of the game, namely several of the explosion particle effects have been redone. Some of the revamped explosion effects sport large protruding clouds of dirt and debris that look more indicative of a grenade blast or a mortar explosion. They are tuned to look a bit more consistent with the overall cartoonish aesthetic of the game. Expect more particle tuning and effects changes in later updates.

[h1]British Voice Overs[/h1]
If you listen closely, you will hear the new British voice overs added in this update. British troops will now spout lines about holding positions, charging the enemy, and throwing grenades, among others. It can be a bit difficult to hear some of these callouts amid the thunderous roar of gunfire and heavy artillery, but when you catch them shouting out how they're out of ammo as they duck for cover, it can add that little bit extra to the experience. 

[h1]Updates to other maps[/h1]
Several of the other maps have seen visual, pathfinding, and gameplay updates, the most noteworth of which are...
[list]
[*]Anzio Day 1 and Day 2 have had their grass and terrain texture work cleaned up. Grass now better aligns with the actual textures on the ground.
[*]Anzio Day 2 has had some of it's capture point boundaries widened, especially those near the river, to allow the allies to capture the point quicker at the game's start.
[*]Port en Bessin (and the night variant) have had their grass cleaned up in some areas, and some of the terrain textures have been tweaked to better match the color of the standing grass.
[*]Port en Bessin has a new capture point in-between the town and the Shore Battery to keep action nearer the center of the map and to incentivize bots to play more near the Shore Battery, as opposed to just the town.
[*]Saint-Aubin-Sur-Mer has had it's pathfinding tweaked to reduce the chances of bots getting stuck on sandbags near the Alley capture point and the Park Battery.
[/list]

[h1]The Future[/h1]
This update will close out larger content delivery for a while (content being maps and larger art assets). Future updates will likely include smaller art assets, but mainly, I intend to focus on gameplay features. In past announcements, I've hinted at scoped weapons, the ability to command troops, and other features, and I'd like to now take a focused swing at those features without the time consumption that developing new maps requires. There are some bugs I'd like to try and squash and some underlying gameplay system that I wish to refactor to allow for more flexibility with future gameplay updates. Stay tuned for more!

As always, I'm humbled to have such a loving community. I wish I could implement every feature request you guys want, but alas, I have to pick what falls within my ability, the game's scope, and what I think aligns best with the gameplay and design of Brass Brigade. But that doesn't mean I don't want to keep hearing from you. Feel free to visit our Discord (link [url=https://discord.gg/DMdGBPc]here[/url]) and the Steam Discussion to drop a line about how you feel about Brass Brigade. 

Until next time,
Henry

notes.title: Battle of Arnhem - Coming Soon!
notes.content:
Happy Weekend Soldiers!

I am thrilled to see so many eager troopers picking up Brass Brigade during this year's Steam Lunar Sale. If you haven't already, right now is a great time to pick up Brass Brigade! As always, I'm thankful to all of you who have already picked it up, provided kind words in your reviews, and offered wonderful feedback that I can use to continue building the game. Cheers to all of you!

[b]This will be a short update on what has been going on and what you can expect in the coming weeks.[/b]


[h1]New Map - Arnhem[/h1]
Operation Market Garden offers many great battles and skirmishes that would be a perfect fit for Brass Brigade (and just about any other WW2 game). It has been immortalized in the classic 1977 film [i]A Bridge Too Far[/i] and serves as the backdrop for the newest addition to the ever-growing map list in Brass Brigade.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/b42ed4bee2b3e326aa6483f9d117a50aa788a981.png[/img]
Specifically, the battle at Arnhem's John Frost bridge will be the centerpiece of the next map. British paratroopers drop from the skies into the fields just outside of the town and must try to advance across the bridge. German troops must spring into a rapid response and try to fend off the advancing British troops. The bridge acts as a large choke-point, with both teams facing a near-certain defeat if their enemy makes it across. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/4a9350aff25403ca5a5f5826af104f768f528d76.png[/img]
Historically, the British failed to hold this bridge while waiting for further allied armored reinforcements. It did in fact prove to be 'a bridge too far,' but will fate play out the same way once your boots are on the ground? Get ready to hold the line soon!
[i]
Shout-out to my buddy Josh for making the beautiful bridge model that serves as the centerpiece of the map!
[/i]

[h1]Other features[/h1]
In the FPS Update Announcement (read it [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1163910/announcements/detail/1710736946839005582]here[/url]), the "Future" section hinted at the Arnhem map. It also mentioned other upcoming gameplay updates, including further first person refinements and issuing commands to your allies. While these are still planned and in development, I don't want to hold up the release of soon-to-be-complete map for features that will still require a reasonable amount of development time. As such, I am planning to release the Arnhem map as soon as it's ready and then continue work on the other features.

[h1]First Person Update Response[/h1]
I'm pleased to see many of you are loving the first person update. Again, it was an entirely experimental feature I added that seemed to work out pretty well. You can see some great gameplay videos here:

notes.title: First Person Mode Update Now Available!
notes.content:
Happy New Year Soldiers!

I hope everyone has had a safe and enjoyable start to their 2020. I wish the best for everyone going into the new decade. It's my pleasure to deliver this new update for Brass Brigade to help welcome in the new year. I hope you enjoy all the new things it brings to the table - without further a-do, let's discuss what's in store.

Here's a quick trailer that covers what's new in the last 2 major updates from this winter: [previewyoutube=DiJ-q0ZeWHI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]First Person Mode[/h1]
As discussed in the previous announcement (read about it [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1163910/announcements/detail/1710736946789247483]here[/url]), players can now switch between the standard third-person camera to a first-person camera. This was more-or-less an experiment that I thought went reasonably well, and while Brass Brigade was never designed as an FPS, it seemed to work well enough that I wanted to keep it in the game. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/5965bf65bc4bd55a5e01d8b1e7762771617fa6c8.png[/img]

By default, press the T key to switch between the modes. The camera will move into your character's head-space and you will get what I describe as an Arma-like FPS mode. The camera isn't perfectly steady - there's weapon sway and slight head sway. It has a rather realistic feeling and offers better indoor navigation and shooting over/around low obstacles. I hope you enjoy this new mode as it grows and is polished more over time. It really transforms the perception and puts you right in the heart of the chaos. 

[h1]New Map - Ponyri Apocalypse[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/323a8448a3e104cc5c910fc23c582776c065f518.png[/img]
The Eastern Front receives a new map in this update as well. Based on the Battle of Ponyri during the Battle of Kursk, Ponyri Apocalypse sees the Red Army fending off an ever-pressing German advance. Burning crop fields and fog disrupt sight lines through the trenches and fields that compose the battlefield. The fighting and body count got so high during the battle that Soviet troops dubbed it the "mini-Stalingrad." 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/e3a104f5fbc62a43117e4f9537e8b00f9c70aa67.png[/img]
The map is rather large and features the most capture points of any Brass Brigade map thus far! There are ten capture points ranging from trench networks, a destroyed German convoy, a downed German transport plane, a dried river bed, a town, and more. Each team starts with 2 entry points into the map and will have to negotiate thick grass, burning debris, soggy marshes, and open fields to get from point to point. It offers everything from close quarters fighting to long range rifle combat. Gear up and try to survive this nearly apocalyptic landscape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/d5ea5cfe451d3d2c92a7c9cc911527b17873e28c.png[/img]

[h1]Persistent Ragdolls[/h1]
By popular request, users can now set the number of bodies that will persist on the battlefield. In the Settings > Gameplay menu, there is now a "Corpse Multiplier" slider that will control the corpse count multiplier. For instance, if you have 10 bots with a corpse multiplier of 2, that means there will be 20 bodies on the ground before they start to get recycled for different corpses. In effect, this means that every bot can get killed twice before a single body would disappear. So for a game of say, 64 bots and a multiplier of 2, there can be up to 128 bodies on the ground at any given time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/a443ded32050e77f854c8f3b4316f34dffdb253b.png[/img]

[b]**This does come with a warning though!**[/b] A large number of ragdolls can cause poor performance. You will need to find a balance for your system and your desired bot counts. Too many ragdolls can result in long load times and sub-par performance, but as is the Brass Brigade mantra - if you can run it, you can have it. [b]Please note also that persistent bodies only work if ragdolls are enabled.[/b]

[h1]Instant Action Custom Presets[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/e4fc24f890c0add4833a3b15ce14e3608ee34177.png[/img]
Another feature added in this update by popular request is the ability to save your configuration of an instant action game. You can then apply that configuration to any other game you like. This will save you time and prevent you from having to re-apply every setting for a battle if you've found a balance you like. Simply save it, and re-select it whenever you wish to apply it! Hopefully this streamlines your experience and simplifies the process of starting a game. 

Update (1/4/2020 2:34 EST) - Presets also carry over from battle to battle when you hit the "Continue to..." button after each game. The main menu "Tank" buttons are also always present now, allowing a team to have tanks IF the map has them. [b]The suggested settings that get applied when selecting a map reflect whether or not each team has tanks to use[/b]. This allows any setting configuration to be applied to any map (ex. avoiding a problem where  a user had a preset with Tanks allowed for the Allies and they attempted to apply it to a map where the Allies had no tanks). 

[h1]Performance and Optimization[/h1]
Some more work has been given to optimization efforts, as discussed in the previous announcement. Perhaps the most effective new option is the ability to disable bullet impact effects. These can have a relatively high CPU cost when there are lots of bots firing in unison. You can disable these effects in the Settings > Graphics & Audio Menu. 

Other under-the-hood optimization work...
[list]
[*] Simplified physics calculations for tanks, increasing performance for maps with lots of tanks
[*] Tweaked bot path-finding to reduce navigation performance costs.
[*] Simplified some particle effects, namely smoke clouds and explosions, to reduce their performance impact.
[*] Reworked bullet & tracer physics which resulted in half the physics cost for projectile based weapons.
[/list]

In the future, I hope to add an option for highly detailed particles, simple particles, and turning-off the bullet impact particles (as is the case now), so users can find a better happy medium, rather than an all-or-nothing approach. But for now, disabling the bullet impact effects when there are high bot counts can buy back a few frames on average. 

[h1]The Future...[/h1]
Because of all these awesome new features listed above, I have afforded myself the framework to add other user requested features. Some of the things that are currently in the works (but not quite ready for this update...) are as follows:
[list]
[*] Sniper Rifles (players will need to be in FPS mode to use the scope)
[*] Further optimization and CPU usage reduction through particle optimization, as current profiler reports indicate that camera rendering cost could be further reduced.
[*] Another new map based on airborne operations...maybe you'll see some paratroopers in the future...who knows?
[*] The ability to issue basic commands to nearby allies, such as following you or attacking a position; this is still highly experimental and conceptual.
[/list]

Here are some teaser images of what may come...
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/2df857c90603c2ffd728a8df99150e83be731566.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/49d6ade5623a1c73604e63b0f970f7d5694dfcc9.png[/img]


Many of these requests are driven by the awesome, constructive feedback that you guys have given me. Feel free to drop more suggestions on the pinned suggestion thread found [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1163910/discussions/0/1742262144180757878/]here[/url].

I hope you enjoy this update and all it has to offer. I look forward to bringing you more throughout 2020. 

Until next time,
Henry K.

notes.title: First Person Mode and More Optimization Coming Soon!
notes.content:
Good day soldiers,

I hope you're all enjoying the Operation Battleaxe update that released a short while ago. I managed to release it ahead of schedule in the hopes of giving everyone some new content for the holiday season. Given the festivities and traveling around this time of year, I knew development would slow a bit and wanted to be sure to deliver Battleaxe in a timely manner. And while the holiday season has indeed slowed my development just a tad, there are definitely new and exciting things coming to Brass Brigade in the near future.

[h1]First Person Mode[/h1]
I was personally a bit skeptical about implementing this, as up to this point in development, I never intended Brass Brigade to be an FPS. However, after a handful of suggestions asking for it, I decided to give it a try, and the results definitely mix-up the Brass Brigade experience - in a good way that is!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/b7c035965c93c740d68f3e8a2210dd985add6ff6.jpg[/img]

Players will now be able to seamlessly switch between the default third-person camera mode and a new first-person camera mode. However,[b] this is not a first person mode akin to most standard FPS games. [/b] The camera literally moves into your character's head space and tracks from that position. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/224bda2bb78ad1ec2c1edf8237018a8a21bb5db2.jpg[/img]

It is a very "immersive" experience similar to how games like ArmA and Post Scriptum handle their first person mode. It makes shooting over obstacles and navigating interior spaces easier since the player does not need to combat the third-person camera in enclosed areas. If nothing else, it provides a very different way of experiencing the battles, at eye level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/f62e4236be56858b7897b78d47c76030cd6c7af6.jpg[/img]

Please note that this mode was more of an experiment gone reasonably well. As such, I am happy to include in into the game, but how much more it gets developed depends entirely on how much I am willing to treat this game as both a third AND first person game. Either way, I hope you enjoy it - I certainly do!



[u][h1]New Optimization & Performance Options[/h1][/u]
Some users are still reporting poor performance even for relatively low bot counts. In an attempt to try and further combat this, some adjustments and options have been made for future builds.
[list]
[*]In the Settings > Graphics and Audio menu, there is a new option called "Bullet Impact Particles". Disabling this will remove the debris and dust that gets kicked up from small-arms gunfire and significantly increases performance for high bot counts.
[*]The bot vision slider has a much greater effect on performance and how far bots can see as the bot count increases. As the bot count increases, bots now see "less far" than they did before, aiding performance.
[*]The bot CPU Time sliders also have a stronger effect on how frequently bots calculate their AI. Reducing this as the bot count increases is strongly recommended, and will automatically occur as the bot count increases. 
[*]Since bots don't collide with one another, their pathfinding was adjusted to ignore finding paths around one another, simplifying pathfinding calculations and mildly increasing performance. 
[/list]

[h1]Optimization Addendum[/h1]
[u][h2]Laptop Performance Tips[/h2][/u]
I've noticed that of the reports of poor performance, it seems that laptops suffer from poor performance more frequently than desktops. Laptops usually have lower performance than their desktop counter-parts, however slight, but the disparity caused me to do some digging into the Unity Engine on laptops.
[list]
[*]For reasons passing understanding, Unity Engine games struggle to properly detect laptop GPU hardware correctly. A preliminary step to potentially boosting performance on laptops is to make sure that your dedicated graphics card is set as the actual graphics device being used when launching Brass Brigade (or other graphics intensive programs for that matter). Guides for how to do this whether you have an AMD or Nvidia graphics card are easily available online.
[*]Be sure your laptop is plugged into a charger.
[*]Make sure your power-plan is set to "High Performance"
[/list]

[u][h2]Unity Engine Benchmarking[/h2][/u]
[i]Please note that the following are my own findings; your results may differ.[/i]

I decided to test Brass Brigade's performance on a laptop equipped with an i7 6600HQ processor, GTX1060 6GB, and 16GB of RAM. With 100 bots, default instant action settings, and the lowest graphics settings, I had an average of 30-50FPS, depending on the map. Maps with more foliage tend to run slower than those without. I could squeeze out about 120-130 bots before the average really started to fall below 30FPS for any map. For reference, the current Steam build as of 12/17/2019 would average no more than 25FPS for any map at only 100 bots. More over, another similarly themed, Battlefield-esque bot FPS game built on the Unity Engine runs at around 30FPS average with around 150 bots on the same machine. On a desktop with an i7 7700k, a GTX1080, and 16GB, the results were a lot better for both. It seems to me that laptop hardware is less forgiving and unfriendly to CPU-intensive games in the Unity Engine.

My Unity profiler tells me that the majority of CPU time is being spent calculating physics and rendering the image to screen; the bot AI is no longer the dominant time-sink. This is what led to the introduction of toggling things like the particle effects, terrain details, etc. I am looking for more options I can introduce to the user so they can tweak the game to find a happy balance between visual fidelity and performance. Back to the Unity Documentation and benchmarks I go! It's worth noting that newer versions of Unity claim to offer better performance for certain things that Brass Brigade relies on, so I am also investigating migrating the project to newer engine versions further in the future. This is a risky proposition though as features I use in the older version may be deprecated in newer versions, requiring rewrites or refactoring just to break even.

[h1]Thanks for your Support[/h1]
I'm glad to see so many people are having fun customizing battles to their liking. Some Youtubers such as GrimyGamer have posted videos showcasing what I suspect are 100-150 bot battles, which you can watch below.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b80rkHNmQyQ

Some other Youtubers such as BaronVonGames and Dragonece Gameplay have made commentary/review videos. I appreciate their kind words and fantastic feedback! Have a listen if you're still on the fence of purchasing Brass Brigade!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=40f5WhCZvRg
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rKarWtFpmxE

I hope you're enjoying the game as much as I've enjoyed making it so far. All of the support and exposure is what helps drive my ability to continue building Brass Brigade. And for that, I offer my sincerest appreciation and gratitude.

[h1]The Future[/h1]
Obviously, all of the aforementioned things are next to be released, but there is more in the way of traditional content being developed too. Additional Eastern Front maps have been requested by many players, so I'm beginning to explore that theater of war a bit more. I'm also drafting new special abilities for the player and conjuring up new weapons. Look for more news of this in the coming weeks.

Enjoy the Holiday Season!
-H.

notes.title: Operation Battleaxe Update Released!
notes.content:
Good day soldiers, 

Today, we see a strong offensive launched on the North African front with the Operation Battleaxe update. In this update, players can find plenty of new features including a new map, a new tank, and more to grow their WWII experience in Brass Brigade!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/4abde4f11a613ef2f991fdc5b9c473cc434c101e.jpg[/img]

[h1]New Map - Operation Battleaxe[/h1]
Operation Battleaxe was teased in a previous post, and it finally arrives in this new update. German and British forces are locked in a fierce battle for the Halfaya Pass in the desert outside Tobruk. The map features the infamous pass as its centerpiece with multiple firebases and supply depots supporting it on either side.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/f87ec3945a27e9e9aa0a92fcb5b86bf275f19648.png[/img]
The map is fairly linear, meaning that teams will need to find flanks on either side to try and punch through the defenses. Either the British will be driven back into the desert or the Germans will be forced into a retreat - gear up and head out into this explosive new map unlike any other found in Brass Brigade thus far!

[h1]New Tank - Panzer IV[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/e9ba0ee6ce18a34e3179b23163c9f69aa7dc570f.png[/img]
A new vehicle joins the German forces in Brass Brigade - the Panzer IV. Perhaps the most well known German tank next to the Tiger, the Panzer IV offers a lower profile, slightly higher top speed, and faster turret, making it a better match for allied armor in more enclosed areas. However, its weaker armor means it can't take as much damage as the Tiger, with the rear being poorly reinforced. The Panzer IV in Brass Brigade comes in two paint schemes - standard and desert. Look for them on maps with German forces!

[h1]Mulitple Tanks per Team[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/8198461353f2a7b469a3a3673fb10ba700801769.png[/img]
Brass Brigade now supports multiple tanks per team on certain maps! On multiple maps, different tanks will spawn for each team, and will continually respawn throughout the game. For example, this means that a battle between the British/American forces and the German forces can see Shermans, Cromwells, Tigers, and Panzers - all in one battle! 

[h1]Leaderboard, Kill Feed, and more![/h1]
Per strong user feedback, an initial implementation of a simple leaderboard for each game has been added. Pressing TAB while playing will open up a leaderboard showing the top performing troops in the game. The same scoreboard, along with the player's personal kill/death ratio is also now shown at the game's conclusion. An optional kill feed is also displayed in the top right of the game, tracking the frags. Set your soldier's name in the settings menu to your liking and it'll appear that way in-game!

[h1]Weapon Accuracy Modifiers[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35926434/90d123d9a4987a6ad2701821d0d127d1df3788d4.png[/img]
Weapons have seen a significant accuracy bump as many players thought the weapons felt 'floaty'. However, you can modify the weapon's global accuracy and damage modifiers in the Settings > Gameplay menu. Feel free to set them to your preference! If you prefer the old weapon accuracy model, just turn it back down all the way to the left.

[h1]Return to Sender![/h1]
Players can now toss back grenades and explosives that land near them. If a grenade lands right at your feet, press the ACTION button (E by default) to throw it back. But be careful, don't get caught by a short fuse!


[h1]The Future[/h1]
I am constantly reading and reviewing the suggestions the community leaves me. There are so many great ideas and features I would love to implement - some of them are already in the works, others are in the prototyping/proof of concept phases. I don't have any more specifics for now, but I am already working on more features to make your experience even more enjoyable.

[h1]Thank you![/h1]
Thanks for supporting Brass Brigade! I'm proud to share my work with all of you and I hope you enjoy this new update as the new year rolls around. Happy Holidays to everyone and here's to 2020!

-Until next time,
Henry

notes.title: Performance & Optimization Boost Incoming!
notes.content:
Hello soldiers!

In response to some initial feedback, some immediate optimization and performance improvements have been made to Brass Brigade. Namely, bot AI has been strongly adjusted so that their artificial intelligence processing is more evenly distributed as the game runs. This means that players should see performance increases across the board.

Please keep in mind that while users should experience a framerate improvement, [b]there will still always exist an upper limit to what your machine can reasonably handle.[/b] You should [b]adjust both the bot counts and CPU Time settings in the instant action menu until you find a balance that you're happy with[/b] - this update should allow you to have a wider window before you feel too much of a performance loss.

So, the overall notes are as follows:

- Optimized bot AI scripts to more evenly distribute load balancing across game simulation time. This can be further controlled by adjusting the CPU Time sliders in the instant action menu for further user control; increasing the CPU Time slider will result in more intelligent and aggressive bot behavior at the expense of performance while decreasing it will result in less intelligent bots while reducing CPU strain and potentially increasing performance.

- When players adjust the bot counts in the main menu, the CPU Time sliders will automatically adjust themselves to a suggested setting to optimize performance experience for desired bot count. The player can them readjust the CPU Time sliders if they wish to override the suggested setting.

With this in mind, I hope this helps Brass Brigade move closer to it's mission of highly customizable match settings. Optimization is always a tricky business, but initial internal testing has shown promise, and I hope you can now share in that performance increase with this update.

With the holiday season here in the United States upon us, updates might slow down for the week (I am the only developer on Brass Brigade). I wish you all a happy Thanksgiving and a wonderful holiday season.

Until next time!
-Henry

PS - Keep the feedback coming! I'll do my best to keep up with the community.
